blocks.text: Need to know how cb source apply takes input; check docs briefly.

text:
Usage: cardboard source apply [options] <project> [file]

Apply a timeline file onto the project as item-level changes

Arguments:
  project          project id, name or bundle path
  file             TSX file, or - for stdin; defaults to the bundle's
                   timeline.tsx

Options:
  --eval           run the file as code (loops, helpers) instead of reading
                   literals; CLI process only
  --prefer <side>  who wins when both changed an item since the file was
                   printed: file (default) or editor
  -h, --help       display help for command

input.command: mkdir -p .scratch && cp timeline.tsx .scratch/w2.tsx && grep -n "cardboard:rev" .scratch/w2.tsx && sed -i '/name="W2"/,/textContent/ s/fontSize={100}/fontSize={321}/' .scratch/w2.tsx && grep -n -A6 'name="W2"' .scratch/w2.tsx
input.description: Copy timeline and set W2 font size in copy

input.command: cb source apply afdced03-331a-4a78-9880-d9895321a71a .scratch/w2.tsx; echo "---"; cat timeline.tsx

blocks.text:
Right after the change, the timeline file shows **W2's font size as 321**, and **the clip on the Mine track is muted** (the 0–3s clip.mp4).

I didn't mute that clip. It wasn't muted in the first printout, but it already was when I read the file again after the ping finished. So the mute came from someone else editing during that wait, even though the file is supposed to hold back other people's changes until my turn ends.

My edit only changed W2's font size. When I made it, I started from that newer copy of the file, so the mute stayed as it was.
